newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to restructure debt to Gazprom in few weeks.
newsitem.headline: Russia to restructure debt to Gazprom in few weeks.

text.p: First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov said on Wednesday that the government would restructure its 10 trillion rouble debt to Gazprom in the next few weeks.

"We will try to do this in the next few weeks and I am pretty sure we will do this," Nemtsov told Reuters during a visit to the central Russian city after being asked whether the government planned to restructure the debt.

Interfax news agency had earlier quoted Nemtsov as saying that the government would sort out the debt in a week and a half's time, after Russia's other First Deputy Prime Minister, Anatoly Chubais, had returned from a summer holiday.

The debt would be turned into government bonds or liquidated via a mutual debt forgiveness operation, Interfax quoted Nemtsov as saying. Russia is mired in a huge non-payments crisis in which many companies owe the government taxes and the government owes them money for services or supplies.
Gazprom, which accounts for a staggering 25 percent of all tax revenues to Russia's state budget, has paid off its tax arrears to the government but still has huge debts.
